In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how the organizational communication of three companies of the Global Pact is oriented to a culture of peace or to the legitimization of organizational violence, in order to contribute to the debate about the role of communication in organizations and its influence in the construction of organizational culture.

The analysis of the three selected videos shows that the companies are not fully aligned with the Global Compact's goals and principles in their institutional communication, as they did not use the elements that could be considered essential for the promotion of the culture of peace, that is to say, dialogue, collective values, social transformation and the historical and socio-cultural context in which they were inserted.
organizational communication is a fundamental tool for the promotion of peace in organizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have sought to understand the communicational actions that can be considered a peace culture, which is a culture that promotes peace and the construction of a world without violence, through the analysis of the institutional speeches of three Brazilian companies that are part of the Global Pact.

organizational communication can and should be oriented to the culture of Peace, which is the opposite of violence, and that this orientation can be identified through the analysis of the institutional discourses of the organizations.

it is necessary to consider a more responsible and ethical communication, in which the organization's institutional communication should be directed towards a culture of peace, in addition to considering the historical and social context in which it is inserted, in order to avoid the legitimization of organizational violence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to identify the presence or absence of communication oriented to the culture of the peace in the institutional speeches of companies, which is essential to understand the role that organizations play in society.

it is possible to understand the importance of communication for the promotion and development of a peace culture in the organizational sphere, as well as to identify the elements that are essential in the construction of a communication that can promote a culture of peace, as well as the problems that can arise from a discourse focused on the legitimation of organizational violence.

organizational communication, especially when referring directly to the institutional positioning of the organization, can influence behaviors, and consequently, in the organization's own culture, and, therefore, it can be considered a strategic element of the organization.
